chapters.title: Work Space Laws
subchapters: Work Space Laws — German employment and workplace law

blocks.text: Our everyday work at LAVA rests on a framework of German employment and workplace law. It protects our health at the desk, in the FabLab and on site, sets the limits of working time and leave, supports us as parents and young colleagues, and guarantees fair treatment for everyone. Click a law to open its official text; copies are also kept in the 5_WORKSPACE LAWS folder on the server.

items.label: Allgemeines Gleichbehandlungsgesetz (AGG)
items.desc: General Equal Treatment Act — protects against discrimination on the grounds of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual identity.

items.label: Arbeitszeitgesetz (ArbZG)
items.desc: Working Hours Act — limits daily working time and sets minimum rest breaks and rest periods between working days.

items.label: Arbeitsgerichtsgesetz (ArbGG)
items.desc: Labour Courts Act — sets out how employment disputes are resolved before the labour courts.

items.label: Arbeitsschutzgesetz (ArbSchG)
items.desc: Occupational Health and Safety Act — obliges the employer to assess the risks of every workplace and take measures to keep employees safe and healthy.

items.label: Arbeitssicherheitsgesetz (ASiG)
items.desc: Occupational Safety Act — requires an occupational safety specialist and a company doctor to advise the employer.

items.label: Arbeitsstättenverordnung (ArbStättV)
items.desc: Workplace Ordinance — requirements for the workplace itself: lighting, ventilation, room temperature, screen work and escape routes.

items.label: Baustellenverordnung (BaustellV)
items.desc: Construction Site Ordinance — how health and safety are planned and coordinated on construction sites.

items.label: Bundeselterngeld- und Elternzeitgesetz (BEEG)
items.desc: Parental Allowance and Parental Leave Act — the right to parental leave and financial support while caring for a child.

items.label: Bundesurlaubsgesetz (BUrlG)
items.desc: Federal Leave Act — the statutory minimum of paid annual leave.

items.label: Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch (BGB) §§611–630
items.desc: Civil Code — §§611–630 define the employment contract and the rights and duties of employer and employee.

items.label: DGUV-Vorschriften
items.desc: Statutory Accident Insurance Regulations — binding accident prevention rules, including the appointment of first aiders and fire safety helpers.

items.label: Heimarbeitsgesetz (HAG)
items.desc: Home Work Act — protection for people who carry out commissioned work from their own premises.

items.label: Jugendarbeitsschutzgesetz (JArbSchG)
items.desc: Protection of Young Workers Act — stricter limits on working hours and tasks for employees under 18, such as interns and apprentices.

items.label: Kündigungsschutzgesetz (KSchG)
items.desc: Protection Against Dismissal Act — protects employees against socially unjustified dismissal.

items.label: Mutterschutzgesetz (MuSchG)
items.desc: Maternity Protection Act — protection periods before and after birth, adapted working conditions and protection against dismissal for pregnant and breastfeeding employees.

items.label: Verordnung über Sicherheit und Gesundheitsschutz bei der Verwendung von Arbeitsmitteln (BetrSichV)
items.desc: Industrial Safety Ordinance — safe use of machines, tools and equipment, as in the FabLab.

blocks.text: This overview is for orientation only and does not replace the legal texts. If you have questions about your rights or obligations, please contact Office Management.

chapters.title: LCA Tools
subchapters: LCA Tools — Life Cycle Assessment software

blocks.text: A Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) measures the environmental impact of a building over its whole life: from extracting and manufacturing the materials, through transport and construction, the years of use and maintenance, to demolition, waste processing and disposal. The main result is the Global Warming Potential (GWP) in kg CO₂-equivalent, which shows how much embodied carbon a design carries.
What an LCA tool does

LCA tools are the software that does this calculation. They take the quantities of a design, from the 3D model or a bill of quantities, and combine them with environmental data for each material, from product-specific EPDs or generic datasets such as ÖKOBAUDAT. The result is broken down by life cycle module following EN 15978, so you can see which elements and materials cause the most impact.

items.v: Raw material supply, transport to the factory and manufacturing.
Transport to site and the construction and installation process.
Use, maintenance, repair, replacement and the building's operational energy and water.
Demolition, transport, waste processing and disposal.
Benefits from reuse, recovery and recycling, reported separately.

blocks.text: When we use them

items: Early design — compare structural systems, materials and massing options while changes are still cheap.
Design development — check that the chosen materials and products keep the project within its carbon target.
Certification and funding — DGNB, QNG and similar schemes require a whole-building LCA.

blocks.text: The tools, licences and guides we use are kept in the 02_LCA tools folder on the server. For the material data that goes into an LCA, see the EPD Databases chapter.

chapters.title: Recommended Materials
subchapters: A Primer on Embodied Carbon — Accepted Manuscript, 2023

blocks.text: An Environmental Product Declaration (EPD) is an independently verified document that reports the environmental impact of a building product over its life cycle, following EN 15804. It is the manufacturer's data sheet for sustainability: it states the Global Warming Potential (GWP) and other indicators per declared unit, such as one m³ of concrete or one m² of insulation, split into the life cycle modules A1–A3, A4–A5, B, C and D.
Why we collect them

EPDs are the input data for every Life Cycle Assessment. The more product-specific EPDs we have, the more accurate our embodied carbon figures are compared with generic datasets, and the easier it is to compare materials and products while designing. EPD databases bring these declarations together so they can be searched by category, manufacturer and impact.
Things to check

items: Declared unit — always compare products per the same unit and quantity.
Validity — EPDs are valid for five years; check the expiry date before using one.
Scope — note which modules are declared; many EPDs cover only A1–A3.
Module D — benefits from reuse and recycling are reported separately and not added to the totals.

blocks.text: Our EPD databases are kept in the LAVA Zero SharePoint. Open them with the EPD Databases OneDrive button.

blocks.text: LAVA was founded in 2007 by Tobias Wallisser, Alexander Rieck and Chris Bosse in Germany and Australia. Today more than 80 people work on projects across Europe, the Middle East, China and Australia.

The practice has developed a specific approach across a wide range of projects of various sizes, cultures and typologies — always driven by intensive dialogue with the client and a commitment to visionary, technology-forward design.
"LAVA is always ready for the next breakthrough!" — Tobias Wallisser, Alexander Rieck, Chris Bosse

blocks.text: Having diverse international perspectives allows for a uniquely strategic approach in masterplanning large-scale developments. High-quality design results from the continuity of the process and intensive dialogue with the client.
"More with Less"

LAVA believes in achieving better quality and better architecture with less material and resources. Every project, in every budget range, incorporates that special, unique LAVA feature — born from ongoing experimentation with materials, technical solutions and methods of production.
"What If?"

At LAVA we ask "What if?" Our practice specialises in finding the core of the client's problem and turning it into a unique advantage. We challenge the perception of architecture as the production of square metres — unifying structure, space and architectural expression to create unique experiences.
LAVA's work is organised around six evolving themes, each framed as an open question:

items: Designed to Connect — What if architecture can enhance a new togetherness of social interaction, lifelong learning and meaningful debate?
Digitizing the Process — What if architecture could gain new relevance by harnessing automation to fight today's housing crisis?
Energy Transition — What if architecture could communicate the abstract nature of energy while being a symbol for a greener future?
Creativity at Work — What if work could be life-improving: making us feel connected, inspired, smarter and more productive?
Future Cities — What if planetary challenges like the climate crisis required new concepts and methods for the architectural profession?
Planning with Nature — What if a single building can be akin to a forest with a highly balanced indoor microbiome to support all species?

a2.title: A.2 Values & General Rules
a2.breadcrumb: Part A — Who We Are > A.2 Values & General Rules
topics: Beliefs applied to office life, not just projects
Equality & respect — regardless of gender, race or position
Knowledge sharing — ask questions, share freely

blocks.text: Office culture is built by the small interactions. Consider the impact that your decisions may have on others.
"The way you do anything is the way you do everything"
It is important that we apply our beliefs to our projects in addition to our office environment. The same values that guide our architecture guide how we work together every day.
Everyone's equality is independent of gender, race or position. Value colleagues and treat them the way you would want to be treated.

items: Treat everyone with equal respect regardless of seniority
Be forward about sharing knowledge and open when you need input
Encourage and accept constructive feedback from anyone

blocks.text: At LAVA we collaborate instead of compete. We encourage sharing constructive feedback and helping each other grow.

items: Share knowledge openly — don't hoard expertise
Ask questions when you need input, and welcome questions directed at you
Give and receive constructive feedback as a normal part of work
Support colleagues across teams and disciplines

blocks.text: Knowledge sharing is one of LAVA's core values. The whole practice improves when individuals share what they know and learn openly.

items: Be proactive about sharing knowledge with colleagues
Ask questions openly — don't struggle alone with a problem
Contribute to Friday Academy and Lunch Presentations
Document project learnings on the server for future teams

blocks.text: It is important for LAVA to support healthy engagement, both in creative work and in how we come together as a community.

items: Fabrication Lab — hands-on making and prototyping
VR-Room — immersive design review and exploration
Monday Morning Meeting — weekly whole-office gathering for connection

blocks.text: These spaces and rituals make LAVA a community, not just a workplace. Make use of them.

b5.title: B.5 Performance & Growth

criteria.name: Interpretation & implementation of project requirements
criteria.plus: Correctly translates the brief and constraints into project deliverables. Requests clarification when requirements are unclear. Integrates changes consistently and in a timely manner.
criteria.minus: Misinterpretation of brief or constraints. Recurrent corrections needed due to incomplete understanding. Late or inconsistent integration of updated requirements.

criteria.name: Planning, execution & adherence to agreed deadlines
criteria.plus: Tasks are delivered within agreed timelines. Work is planned realistically according to project phases. Delays are anticipated and communicated early.
criteria.minus: Deadlines are frequently missed. Planning does not reflect actual workload or priorities. Delays are communicated late or not at all.

criteria.name: Level of independent task execution
criteria.plus: Assigned tasks are completed independently within role scope. Appropriate escalation when issues exceed responsibility. Limited supervision required.
criteria.minus: Tasks require frequent follow-up or rework. Difficulty progressing without close supervision. Issues not escalated in time.

criteria.name: Design Quality
criteria.plus: Design output meets project objectives and office standards. Proposals are coherent, buildable, and appropriate to context. Design decisions are clearly articulated.
criteria.minus: Design output lacks consistency or clarity. Solutions do not fully respond to constraints. Frequent revisions required to reach expected quality.

criteria.name: Technical Knowledge, codes & standards
criteria.plus: Applies relevant technical principles and regulations correctly. Anticipates technical implications of design decisions. Knows when to consult specialists.
criteria.minus: Gaps in technical understanding affect project quality. Recurrent errors related to codes or standards. Technical risks not identified early.

criteria.name: Tools
criteria.plus: Uses required tools efficiently and according to office standards. Files are structured, coordinated, and reusable. Keeps up with required tool updates.
criteria.minus: Inefficient or inconsistent use of tools. Non-compliance with file or documentation standards. Work requires technical correction by others.

criteria.name: Communication & coordination
criteria.plus: Information is communicated clearly and in a timely manner. Coordination with team members and consultants is effective. Feedback is integrated appropriately.
criteria.minus: Information gaps or misunderstandings affect coordination. Feedback is integrated late or incompletely. Communication causes avoidable rework.

criteria.name: Participation in assigned project activities
criteria.plus: Participates in required meetings and coordination activities. Follows up on agreed actions. Contributes constructively within assigned scope.
criteria.minus: Inconsistent participation in required activities. Follow-up on actions is incomplete. Responsibilities are not fully carried through.

criteria.name: Proactive contribution within role scope
criteria.plus: Identifies issues related to own tasks early. Proposes solutions or alternatives within role scope. Supports smooth project progress.
criteria.minus: Issues are addressed only after escalation. Limited anticipation of project needs. Opportunities for improvement are not communicated.

categories.label: Professional Conduct in the Work Context

criteria.name: Compliance with professional standards
criteria.plus: Adheres to internal rules, procedures and professional norms. Conduct in work situations is appropriate and consistent. Represents the office professionally.
criteria.minus: Inconsistent adherence to procedures or standards. Professional conduct requires repeated clarification. Misalignment with office working practices.

criteria.name: Availability during agreed working hours
criteria.plus: Is reachable during agreed working hours (9:30–18:00). Participates in required meetings. Responds within reasonable timeframes.
criteria.minus: Availability is inconsistent with agreed arrangements. Delayed responses impact coordination. Missed meetings without adequate communication.

criteria.name: Continuity of project work
criteria.plus: Work continuity is ensured through documentation and handover. Unavailability is communicated in advance when possible. Projects progress smoothly despite absences.
criteria.minus: Lack of handover affects project progress. Information gaps arise during unavailability. Continuity relies excessively on others stepping in.

blocks.text: Application for Leave

When you decide to leave LAVA, the process begins with a formal application for leave. This document is required to officially initiate your departure and must be submitted to your line manager and HR as early as possible.

items: Complete the Application for Leave form and submit it to your direct manager
Send a copy to administration (HR) for processing
Your notice period begins from the date the application is received and acknowledged
Keep a copy of the signed and confirmed application for your own records

blocks.text: The Application for Leave form is available on the server — use the server link button on the left to copy the path.

c1.title: C.1 Office Rules
c1.breadcrumb: Part C — The Office Environment > C.1 Office Rules
topics: Desks & workstations — allocated vs rotating, the Hub
Access & security — locking, alarm, door code
Check-in / check-out system — shared resources & equipment

blocks.text: The Hub has wooden drawers stocked with cables, webcams and other tech devices. Stationery and office supplies can be found in the closets by administration.
Ask administration if you need anything — they are the first point of contact for all office supplies and equipment.
Each team is responsible for the windows along their "island". The last team member — not the last person to leave the office — closes these windows.
If the last person in the office has to close a window that belongs to another team, take a snapshot — that team buys a drink!
All other windows (green room, meeting rooms etc.) must be closed by the last user when they leave. These windows should never be left open when nobody is in the room.
It is everyone's duty to answer the phone. Introduce yourself professionally: say "LAVA Berlin" and your name. If you take a message, write down the caller's name and company and forward it promptly.
If you accept a package at the door, either bring it directly to the addressed person or deliver it to Administration so that it can be forwarded correctly.
Never leave packages unattended at the entrance.
Reimbursement
LAVA covers all work-related expenses you incur on behalf of the office. The following costs are fully reimbursable when accompanied by a receipt and submitted within 30 days of the expense date.

items: MMM (Monday Morning Meeting) — catering, refreshments and any supplies purchased for the weekly team meeting
Overnight dinners — meals during business trips or client events that extend past regular working hours
Taxi & transport — rides to/from client sites, airports, or off-site meetings when public transport is impractical
Project expenses — materials, printing, models, or other direct project costs approved by the project lead
Travel — flights, trains, hotels, and ground transport for work-related travel

blocks.text: Keep all original receipts. Expenses submitted without proof of purchase cannot be processed.

c2.title: C.2 Housekeeping
c2.breadcrumb: Part C — The Office Environment > C.2 Housekeeping
topics: Cleaning schedule — twice weekly, Friday tidy

blocks.text: A cleaning service comes to the office twice per week. On top of this, everyone is expected to keep their workspace tidy and act proactively.

items: Do not leave things on the floor before the cleaning service visits
Leave workstations in the state you found them — including cables and peripherals
Tidy and clean your desk every Friday before leaving
Replace shared items (like hand towels) when you finish them — don't leave it for the next person

blocks.text: There is one dishwasher. Put all glasses, cups, plates and cutlery straight into the dishwasher throughout the day. Turn it on when full; unload when the cycle completes.

items: If you have a meeting with consultants or clients: clean the table and do the washing up immediately after — do not leave anything for others
Do not leave dirty dishes in the sink
Keep the fridge presentable and clear out old food

blocks.text: The kitchen is a shared space — leave it at least as clean as you found it.
There is a rotating weekly list of Kitchen Duty responsibilities. Check the planning to know when it is your week.
Weekly duties include:

items: Briefly wiping down kitchen surfaces before signing off for the day
Making sure the fridge is presentable

blocks.text: LAVA supports bringing fruit or snacks to leave in public areas, and will reimburse you for office purchases.
Reimbursement process:

items: Send an email to admin with the filled-out reimbursement form and a copy of receipts
Submit physical receipts to admin for record keeping

blocks.text: The reimbursement form is available in the IT Wiki: Teams > BER > Office Management > IT Wiki
Have a forward-thinking approach to maintaining the office. If you notice something that needs attention, take care of it or report it.

items: Report broken, missing or needed items to administration immediately
If you take the last snack or finish the coffee pot, take care of the empty dish
If you see something that should be taken care of and don't know how, reach out to admin

blocks.text: There are four bins in the kitchen. Please use them correctly for waste separation:

items.v: Restmüll — general waste
Gelber Sack — plastics, cartons, packaging
Papiertonne — paper, cardboard, newspapers
Small organic bin in the kitchen — food scraps only

blocks.text: Bokashi Composting

As part of LAVA's sustainability initiative, we use Bokashi composting — an airtight fermentation process. Do not open the Bokashi bins (they smell due to rapid decomposition). Use the small organic bin instead; admin handles the transfer to the Bokashi container.

blocks.text: LAVA's library contains books and the most important architecture and design magazines. Research is a core part of the creative design process — books offer better quality information than a quick internet search.
Library categories

items: Projects & Collections (World, Asia, Europe, Germany, Berlin)

blocks.text: Current periodicals

items: Detail · AIT · Interior/Fashion · Der Architekt · DAB

blocks.text: To borrow a book: fill out the Book Borrowing form with your name and the book title, and give it to the Office Manager so others can find it.
Safety First
Always prioritise safety in the Fabrication Lab. A First Aid Kit is always nearby — find it before you start work. Wear appropriate protective gear (gloves, safety goggles, air-purifying masks).
General rules

items: Treat all tools, equipment and machines with care and respect
Always clean up after finishing and return tools and materials to their designated places
Certain machines require authorisation and training — never use them without prior approval or without an authorised person present
Report any damage, malfunction or burnt smell to Office Management immediately
Always use scrap materials before opening new stock
Log used materials on the online list provided by Office Management

blocks.text: In case of injury: call 112. In case of fire: use the extinguisher and call 112 if needed. Never use equipment you have not been trained on.
Meeting rooms are available for internal design meetings and external consultations. The person who arranges the meeting is responsible for preparing the room.
Room booking

items: Book via the Office Calendar in Outlook — specify Meeting Room 1 or Meeting Room 2
This ensures other meetings can be scheduled around free slots
Ask IT for help with Outlook calendar booking if needed

blocks.text: Hosting a meeting

items: Prepare laptop and screen yourself before guests arrive
Set up coffee, tea and water with glasses
After the meeting: clear and tidy the room for the next guests

blocks.text: Friday Academy

On some Friday afternoons, time is set aside from ongoing projects to work, share and learn as a small group — for example: learning a software tool, developing an office standard, or writing a shared script.
Think about what skill or knowledge you have and would like to share with others.
Friday Lunch Presentations
On some Fridays, a colleague presents over lunch — a competition debrief, a project phase review, or a specific technical or research topic.
The goal is not just to present a project, but to share learning: LAVA's design strategy, competition booklet development, drawing techniques, research approaches.
Pin-up

Pin-up panels in the Flex Room display projects in progress. LAVA encourages teams to pin up in-progress material to share their work with the whole office. There is no fixed format — it rotates as projects evolve.

d1.title: D.1 Work Safety
d1.breadcrumb: Part D — Safety & Environment > D.1 Work Safety
topics: Safety roles — Sicherheitsfachkraft, Sicherheitsbeauftragte, Brandschutzhelfer, Ersthelfer

blocks.text: LAVA maintains designated safety roles in the Berlin office, as required by German occupational safety law (Arbeitssicherheitsgesetz):

items.v: Safety specialist — responsible for occupational health and safety oversight
Safety officer — practical safety representative in the office
Fire protection helper — trained in fire evacuation procedures
First aider — trained in first aid and emergency response

blocks.text: Names and contact details for current role holders are available from Office Management.
In any emergency — call 112 (police, fire brigade, ambulance)

items.v: Ask colleagues for help. Use the First Aid Kit. If the kit is not sufficient, call 112 immediately.
Locate the nearest fire extinguisher and use it if safe to do so. Evacuate. Call 112 for a large fire.
Notify Office Management and your Project Lead immediately, and log the incident.

blocks.text: A First Aid Kit is always nearby in the Fabrication Lab. Locate it before starting work so you know exactly where it is in case of need.

items: First Aid Kit — located in the Fabrication Lab
Fire Extinguisher — located near the Fabrication Lab entrance

blocks.text: Familiarise yourself with the location of safety equipment on your first visit to the FabLab.
If you notice any hazard, damage or malfunction anywhere in the office or Fabrication Lab, report it to Office Management immediately. Do not wait, and do not continue to use damaged equipment.

items: Damaged tools or machines — stop use immediately and report to Office Management
Burnt smell or unusual noise from equipment — stop use and report
Trip hazards, spills or structural issues — report immediately

blocks.text: The Berlin server follows a standardised folder structure shared with the Stuttgart office. Familiarise yourself with the layout and consult the PowerPoint folder structure guide.

items.v: \\lava-b-stor01\LIBRARY\1_LAVA\LAVA STANDARDS\FOLDER STRUCTURE

blocks.text: LAVA has released a new unified folder structure. All new projects in both Berlin and Stuttgart must use this structure from now on.
The Berlin server (\\lava-b-stor01) is divided into the following main zones:

items.v: All ongoing and recent Berlin projects — categorised by number and abbreviation. DO NOT MOVE OR DELETE FILES.
Reference materials, standards and resources accessible to everyone. DO NOT MOVE OR DELETE FILES.
Temporary files only — emptied regularly. Do not store anything important here.
Scanned documents from the printer. Delete your scans from this folder after use.

blocks.text: BER LIBRARY sub-folders

items: 1. LAVA — logos, office manual, standards and project structure guides
2. FUNDAMENTALS — readings, guidelines, regulations and references
3. RESOURCES — software tools, fonts and tutorials
4. PRODUCTS — supplier catalogues and product references (add new ones as you use them)

blocks.text: Each project on the server is saved under a unique number with an abbreviation as its name. All projects share the same standardised internal folder structure.

Project numbers are created by the Project Lead at the start of a project. New project numbers are decided and coordinated exclusively during the Monday Morning Meeting — also coordinated with Stuttgart.

The Project Database stores only key files for the website, publications and portfolio — not the full project archive. All relevant information must be saved there before taking compensation days, going on holiday or starting a new project.
Steps for archiving a project phase

items: Create a folder with the phase name
Original Files: save final presentation as packaged InDesign or PPT; include original AI, PS, JPEG, PDF, movie files and physical model photos
Publication: save ONLY the most relevant images, plans and diagrams in JPEG or PDF — curated selection, not everything
In Publication > Text folder: use the Card template to enter all project info

blocks.text: No Rhino, Revit or other raw working files belong in the database. Only final, publication-quality content.

g1.title: G.1 Knowledge & Growth
g1.breadcrumb: Part G — Knowledge & Growth > G.1 Knowledge & Growth
topics: Internal knowledge sharing — pin-up culture, project reviews

blocks.text: On some Friday afternoons, time is set aside from ongoing projects to work, share and learn as a small group. This can be regular — for example: learning a software, developing an office standard, or building a shared script.
Think about what skill or expertise you have and would like to share with others. Everyone has something to contribute.
Friday Academy is a community investment — the whole office improves when individuals share what they know.
On some Fridays, colleagues present a topic over lunch — a competition debrief after submission, a project phase review, a specific technical subject, or a research area.

The goal is not simply to present a project, but to share learning: how LAVA develops a design strategy, how we put together a competition booklet, how we draw a detail, how we push research on a topic.
Lunch Presentations give the whole team access to the thinking behind the work — not just the result.
Pin-up
The Flex Room has Pin-up panels displaying projects in progress. LAVA encourages all teams to pin up in-progress material to share current development with the wider office.
There is no fixed format. It rotates naturally as projects evolve — new material replaces older work. If your project is at an interesting stage, put it up.
Pin-up culture is a direct expression of LAVA's belief in knowledge sharing and open studio practice.
